$comment: Shared state for ONE work-graph run. Lives at .graph/runs/<run-id>/state.json. Every node reads this on start and appends to its OWN key on finish - the builder writes its own builders.<slice> key, including the branch it worked on. Never rewrite another node's key. Every node key carries written_by, naming the node that wrote it: that is the ONLY record of authorship this file has, and without it 'never rewrite another node's key' is unverifiable - an orchestrator hand-writing all six keys is indistinguishable from six nodes doing their jobs. verify-state.py --audit checks it. This file is the edge: it is how context crosses between agents that cannot see each other.
goal: one sentence, in the user's words
status: scouting | planning | awaiting-approval | building | reviewing | integrating | done | blocked

scout.written_by: the node that wrote this key - here, always the string scout
facts: verified statements about what exists today, each with a file:line
unknowns: questions the plan must answer or assume

architect.written_by: the node that wrote this key - here, always the string architect
architect.rationale: why this shape and not the cheaper one

scope_exceptions: ORCHESTRATOR-OWNED, normally empty. Paths a builder may write that the approved plan does not list. guard-builder-scope.py DENIES a builder's Write/Edit outside architect.plan[].files, and this is the only way through it. Adding one is a deliberate, recorded act: pair it with deviation_from_approved_plan on the slice that needed it, and say why the gate's file set was wrong. Never add a path to silence the guard on work the human did not approve.

s1.written_by: the node that wrote this key - here, always the string builder, never orchestrator
s1.branch: written by the builder: the branch this slice's work landed on, or an empty string when the target is not a git repo at all
s1.gate_results: optional: this slice's done_when commands paired with their actual output, when worth keeping verbatim
s1.deviation_from_approved_plan: optional: set only when the orchestrator authorized work outside the architect's approved file set or intent for this slice, and why

s1.$comment: RE-REVIEWS NEST, and this is the rule every reader follows. The TOP LEVEL of reviews.<slice> IS attempt 1. A re-review writes attempt_2, then attempt_3, and so on, each with the same fields as the top level. Every attempt SURVIVES PERMANENTLY - history is never overwritten, flattened, or migrated up. The LATEST attempt supplies the verdict: that is what close-run.py, brief.py and verify-state.py resolve through, and what the board's finalVerdict() has always shown. `ever_rejected` - did ANY attempt REJECT - is DISPLAY ONLY, forever, so a rejection stays visible after it is fixed; it must never gate anything, or the fleet stops being able to loop. NO NODE MAY REWRITE AN EARLIER ATTEMPT: a second reviewer writes its own attempt_N and leaves the ones before it alone, top-level verdict included - relocating that verdict would destroy the history the board keeps and leave a key stamped written_by:reviewer with someone else as its real author. The KEY INDEX numbers an attempt, not the `attempt` field inside it; the field is display. An EMPTY attempt_N is not a re-review, it is a key nobody wrote - write the whole attempt or none of it. The walk STOPS AT THE FIRST GAP, so an attempt_3 with no attempt_2 is ignored and the earlier verdict stands: A GAP IS MALFORMED AND NO NODE MAY LEAVE ONE. Write the next UNUSED N and never skip - a mis-numbered re-review is not reported anywhere, it is simply unread, and a REJECT nobody reads is a REJECT nobody acts on. The cap is attempt_9, matching the board's `for (i = 2; i < 10; i++)` exactly so the two readers cannot disagree; attempt_10 and beyond is reported loudly and resolved by nobody.
s1.written_by: the node that wrote this key - here, always the string reviewer, never the builder it is reviewing
s1.summary: optional: one paragraph a human can read without opening findings[]

findings.origin: optional: scout|architect|builder|'' - which upstream node's miss this traces to, per reviewer.md's failure-mode triage. Blank when a finding doesn't trace to one node cleanly

attempt_2.written_by: the node that wrote this key - here, always the string reviewer, and never the reviewer of an earlier attempt
attempt_2.summary: optional: one paragraph a human can read without opening findings[]

findings.origin: optional: scout|architect|builder|'' - which upstream node's miss this traces to, per reviewer.md's failure-mode triage. Blank when a finding doesn't trace to one node cleanly

integrator.written_by: the node that wrote this key - here, always the string integrator
integrator.verification: what command proved it works, and its output

ops.written_by: the node that wrote this key - here, always the string ops

log: append-only: node, what it did, timestamp
